newsitem.title: PERU: Lima stocks mixed as Telefonica draws interest.
newsitem.headline: Lima stocks mixed as Telefonica draws interest.

text.p: The Lima Stock Exchange ended mixed Wednesday on improved trading volume marked by strong investor interest in benchmark Telefonica del Peru, brokers said.
They predicted stable trading Thursday as investor concerns over internal politics fade and Peru's strong economic fundamentals gradually come to the fore again.

According to preliminary figures, the bolsa's General Index edged down 0.1 percent to 2,161.88 points while the blue-chip index gained 0.38 percent to 3,122.53 on volume of 48 million soles ($18.1 million) in 2,113 operations.
Telefonica gained 2.77 percent to 7.06 soles, in part due to recommendations from investment banks.

"The trading started very slowly, but at the close the number of operations increased due to requests for Telefonica," which accounted for 25 percent of total volume, said Luis Rojas, of Investa brokerage.

Polymetallic miner Volcan's common shares enjoyed a 7.42 percent rise to 15.20 soles, while its labor stock gained 5.59 percent to 15.10 soles on rumors of a possible injection of capital from a foreign investor, brokers added.

Among losers, electricity company Edegel fell 1.48 percent to 1.33 soles, while miner Minsur was off 2.38 percent to 10.25 soles and another miner, Morococha MORt.LMM, dipped 0.94 percent to 6.29 soles.
"The market is quiet at the moment ... until the latest macroeconomic figures for inflation and gross domestic product (GDP) appear," said another broker.
Among 87 stocks traded, 30 fell, 29 were flat and 28 rose.
